He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Buffalo Bulls men's basketball|Buffalo Bulls]]. ==High school career== Graves was born in [[Canton, Ohio]] but grew up in [[Malvern, Ohio]]. He began playing basketball at the age of six and was also a star player in baseball and football.{{cite news |last1=McCleary |first1=Michael |title=Jayvon Graves, from Akron, Ohio to Buffalo is building a legacy for himself |url=http://dailyorange.com/2017/12/jayvon-graves-akron-ohio-buffalo-building-legacy/ |accessdate=April 17, 2020 |work=The Daily Orange |date=December 25, 2017 |archive-date=January 8, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200108221519/http://dailyorange.com/2017/12/jayvon-graves-akron-ohio-buffalo-building-legacy/ |url-status=live }} He attended [[St. Vincent–St. Mary High School]] where he was coached by [[Dru Joyce II]].{{cite news |last1=Beaven |first1=Michael |title=Buffalo's Jayvon Graves of Malvern enters NBA Draft |url=https://www.cantonrep.com/sports/20200325/buffalorsquos-jayvon-graves-of-malvern-enters-nba-draft |accessdate=April 17, 2020 |work=[[Canton Repository]] |date=March 25, 2020 |archive-date=March 29, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200329102331/https://www.cantonrep.com/sports/20200325/buffalorsquos-jayvon-graves-of-malvern-enters-nba-draft |url-status=dead }} As a senior, he helped St. Vincent-St. Mary to its first state title since 2011 and 25–5 record. He scored 22 points and grabbed 10 rebounds in the title game.{{cite news |last1=DeCicco |first1=Anthony |title=A quiet leader |url=https://www.ubspectrum.com/article/2019/12/a-quiet-leader |accessdate=April 17, 2020 |work=Buffalo Spectrum |date=December 5, 2019 |archive-date=April 16, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200416225347/https://www.ubspectrum.com/article/2019/12/a-quiet-leader |url-status=live }} Graves averaged 21.5 points, 4.9 rebounds, and 2.5 assists per game. He shared All-Ohio Player of the Year honors in Division II with [[Trotwood High School]]'s Torrey Patton, and Graves was named cleveland.com Boys Basketball Player of the Year.{{cite news |last1=Goul |first1=Matt |title=Meet cleveland.com's 2016-17 boys basketball all-stars |url=https://www.cleveland.com/hssports/blog/2017/04/fabulous_50_meet_clevelandcoms.html |accessdate=April 6, 2020 |work=[[The Plain Dealer]] |date=April 12, 2017 |archive-date=April 6, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200406195138/https://www.cleveland.com/hssports/blog/2017/04/fabulous_50_meet_clevelandcoms.html |url-status=live }} In AAU play, he competed for the King James Shooting Stars. Graves was a three-star recruit with offers from 13 schools, including MAC schools [[Toledo Rockets men's basketball|Toledo]] and [[Kent State Golden Flashes men's basketball|Kent State]], but signed with [[Buffalo Bulls men's basketball|Buffalo]]. He said he was drawn to the Bulls because of "the style of play, the atmosphere, closeness to home and the coaching staff," particularly [[Nate Oats]].{{cite news |last1=Weiss |first1=Justin |title=Draft dreams: Jayvon Graves mulls NBA future |url=https://www.ubspectrum.com/article/2020/03/draft-dreams-jayvon-graves-mulls-nba-future |accessdate=April 17, 2020 |work=Buffalo Spectrum |date=March 25, 2020 |archive-date=April 16, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200416223705/https://www.ubspectrum.com/article/2020/03/draft-dreams-jayvon-graves-mulls-nba-future |url-status=live }} ==College career== As a freshman, Graves played in all 36 games and averaged 5.1 points and 2.3 rebounds per-game. He helped the team finish 27–9 and defeat [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]] in the first round of the NCAA Tournament. As a sophomore, he became a starter, contributing 9.7 points and 4.2 rebounds per game. Graves helped the Bulls finish a school-record 32–4 and defeat [[Arizona State Sun Devils men's basketball|Arizona State]] in the first round of the NCAA Tournament before losing to eventual national runner-up [[Texas Tech Red Raiders men's basketball|Texas Tech]].{{cite news |last1=Beaven |first1=Michael |title=Former St. V-M star Jayvon Graves enters NBA Draft, maintains college eligibility |url=https://www.beaconjournal.com/sports/20200325/former-st-v-m-star-jayvon-graves-enters-nba-draft-maintains-college-eligibility |accessdate=April 17, 2020 |work=[[Akron Beacon-Journal]] |date=March 25, 2020 |archive-date=March 28, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200328000657/https://www.beaconjournal.com/sports/20200325/former-st-v-m-star-jayvon-graves-enters-nba-draft-maintains-college-eligibility |url-status=dead }} His best game as a sophomore came on February 19, 2019, when he tallied 26 points in a 114–67 blowout win over [[Ohio Bobcats men's basketball|Ohio]].{{cite news |title=No. 25 Buffalo stampedes Ohio for 23rd straight home win |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401087409 |accessdate=April 17, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=February 19, 2019 |archive-date=March 15, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190315071043/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401087409 |url-status=live }} Coming into his junior season, Graves was the leading returning scorer on a team that lost [[C. J. Massinburg]], [[Nick Perkins]] and [[Jeremy Harris (basketball)|Jeremy Harris]] to graduation. On February 21, 2020, Graves scored a career-high 33 points in a 104–98 double overtime win at [[Kent State Golden Flashes men's basketball|Kent State]]. As a junior, Graves led Buffalo in scoring at 17.1 points per game in addition to averaging 5.4 rebounds and 2.5 assists per game in 32 games, all starts. He set the program record for field goals attempted in a season with 479, and his 204 made field goals are third highest in a season at Buffalo. He was named to the First Team All-[[Mid-American Conference|MAC]]. Following the season, he declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]] but did not hire an agent. On June 6, Graves announced he was withdrawing from the draft and returning to Buffalo.{{cite news |last1=Beaven |first1=Michael |title=Jayvon Graves withdraws from NBA Draft, returning to Buffalo for senior year |url=https://www.cantonrep.com/sports/20200606/jayvon-graves-withdraws-from-nba-draft-returning-to-buffalo-for-senior-year |accessdate=August 2, 2020 |work=[[Canton Repository]] |date=June
